info.name: Agreed API
info.description:
The Agreed API is organized around REST. It has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON-encoded request bodies (OAuth endpoints also accept form-encoded bodies), returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP response codes and verbs.

**Base URL:** `https://agreed.net`

## We support two integration pathways

1. **Zapier, ChatGPT, Claude and other apps:** OAuth 2.0 (authorization code flow, with refresh tokens).
2. **Custom scripts and direct API requests:** a personal API key (Bearer token).

---

## 🔑 Authentication

Every API request sends a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The token is either an **OAuth access token** (starts with `agrat_`) or a **personal API key** (starts with `agr_`). Both identify the same Agreed account and have the same access.

### 1. Personal API key

For scripts or direct REST requests.

**How to get your API key:**
1. Log in to your Agreed account.
2. Go to **Settings → Integrations → Claude**.
3. Create a new key and copy it. It is shown only once.
4. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer agr_…`

Keys don't expire. Delete a key in the same place to revoke it.

### 2. OAuth 2.0 (Zapier and other apps)

Agreed is a standard OAuth 2.0 authorization server.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Discovery document | `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` |
| Authorization URL | `https://agreed.net/oauth/authorize` |
| Token URL | `https://agreed.net/api/oauth/token` |
| Revocation URL | `https://agreed.net/api/oauth/revoke` |
| Scope | `mcp` |
| Grant types | `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` |
| PKCE | `S256`. Required for public clients (no secret); optional for confidential clients (with a client secret) |
| Access token lifetime | 1 hour (`expires_in: 3600`) |
| Refresh token lifetime | 30 days. Refresh tokens rotate: each refresh returns a new pair and the old refresh token stops working |

**Flow:**
1. Send the user to the Authorization URL. They sign in to Agreed and click **Allow** on the consent screen.
2. Agreed redirects back to your `redirect_uri` with `?code=…&state=…`.
3. Exchange the code at the Token URL for an `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
4. Call the API with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. When it expires, use the refresh token.

Users can disconnect an app at any time in **Settings → Integrations**.

---

## ⚡ Webhooks (instant triggers)

Subscribe a URL to an event and Agreed sends a `POST` to it with JSON every time the event happens.

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `document.viewed` | A recipient opened the document for the first time |
| `document.signed` | A recipient finished signing their part |
| `document.completed` | Every recipient has signed |

**Delivery:**
- `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `User-Agent: Agreed-Webhooks/1.0`
- Headers `X-Agreed-Event` (event type), `X-Agreed-Delivery` (delivery id), `X-Agreed-Signature`
- Any 2xx response counts as delivered. Otherwise Agreed retries after 5 seconds and again after 30 seconds. The timeout is 10 seconds per attempt.
- Each event is sent once per subscription. Use the payload `id` to de-duplicate.

**Signature:** `X-Agreed-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1 = HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")`. The signing secret of an endpoint is shown in **Settings → Integrations → Webhooks**.

**Payload:**
```json
{
  "id": "cmwsy9ji40001jzeyuno2yuxp",
  "type": "document.signed",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-23T07:34:09.917Z",
  "data": {
    "document": { "id": "…", "name": "Non-Disclosure Agreement", "status": "sent", "url": "https://agreed.net/documents/…" },
    "recipient": { "id": "…", "email": "jane@example.com", "firstName": "Jane", "lastName": "Doe", "viewedAt": "…", "signedAt": "…" }
  }
}
```
`document.completed` has no `recipient` object.

---

## Errors

Errors return a JSON body `{ "error": "...", "error_description": "..." }` (or `{ "error": "..." }`).

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 / 201 | Success |
| 400 | Invalid request (missing or wrong parameters) |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`invalid_token`) or bad client credentials (`invalid_client`) |
| 404 | Not found |
| 429 | Too many requests. Slow down and retry |
| 500 | Something went wrong on our side |

## Rate limits

- Token endpoint: 60 requests per minute per IP
- Webhook subscriptions: 30 per minute per account; at most 50 webhook endpoints per account

item.description: Standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow. These requests don't use the Bearer token.

request.description: OAuth 2.0 server metadata (RFC 8414): every endpoint URL and the supported grants, PKCE methods and scopes.

query.description: Must exactly match a redirect URI registered for the client.
Opaque value returned unchanged. Use it to prevent CSRF.
PKCE challenge: base64url(SHA-256(code_verifier)). Required for public clients; optional when you have a client secret.

request.description:
Open this URL **in a browser**. It isn't an API call. The user signs in to Agreed (if needed) and sees a consent screen. On **Allow**, Agreed redirects to:

```
{redirect_uri}?code=agrac_…&state=random-state-123
```

On **Deny**: `{redirect_uri}?error=access_denied&state=…`

The code is single-use and expires after 10 minutes.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description: REST-hook subscriptions for instant triggers. See the collection overview for the payload format and signature.

request.description:
Registers a URL to receive one event type (REST hook). Keep the returned `id`; you need it to unsubscribe.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `hookUrl` | string, required | Public `https://` URL that receives the POSTs. (`url` is accepted as an alias.) |
| `event` | string, required | `document.viewed`, `document.signed` or `document.completed` |

The subscription also appears in **Settings → Integrations → Webhooks**, where the user can see deliveries or remove it.

response.name: 400 Bad request

request.description: Removes a subscription by the `id` returned from Subscribe. It succeeds even if the subscription is already gone.

Returns up to 3 recent events of that type for the account, newest first, in exactly the webhook payload format. With no events yet, it returns one example event. Use it to map fields before a real event arrives.

item.name: Zapier
item.description:
The requests the **Agreed Zapier integration** makes, one folder per trigger. Authentication is the OAuth 2.0 flow in *Authentication (OAuth 2.0)* (Zapier sends `Authorization: Bearer {{bundle.authData.access_token}}` on every request).

To try these in Postman, set `zapierHookUrl` in the environment to any URL that accepts POSTs (e.g. a webhook.site URL), and `hookId` to the `id` returned by Subscribe.

request.description:
**Zapier:** Authentication → Step 5 "Test your Authentication".

Zapier calls this after the user connects Agreed. The connection is labelled with `{{bundle.inputData.email}}`.

item.name: Trigger: Document Completed
item.description:
**Zapier trigger** `document_completed` (REST Hook): Triggers when every recipient has signed a document.

| Zapier setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | `document_completed` |
| Label | Document Completed |
| Subscribe | `POST /api/v1/hooks` with body `hookUrl = {{bundle.targetUrl}}`, `event = document.completed` |
| Unsubscribe | `DELETE /api/v1/hooks/{{bundle.subscribeData.id}}` |
| Perform List | `GET /api/v1/hooks/sample?event=document.completed` |
| Perform | Default (the webhook body as-is) |

request.description: Zapier sends this when a user turns on a Zap that uses **Document Completed**. In Zapier the body is `{ "hookUrl": "{{bundle.targetUrl}}", "event": "document.completed" }`. The returned `id` becomes `{{bundle.subscribeData.id}}`.
Zapier sends this when the Zap is turned off or deleted. In Zapier the URL is `/api/v1/hooks/{{bundle.subscribeData.id}}`.
Zapier calls this to load sample **Document Completed** events while the user maps fields in the Zap editor.
